transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Iran continues to target ships traversing the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran's trying to block U.S. efforts to guide vessels carrying oil through the key waterway.
NPR's Hadil Al-Shelchi reports.
Iran has intensified its attacks on ships trying to cross the Strait of Hormuz without
its permission.
On Wednesday, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said that a cargo ship sank after
hitting a naval mine.
Iran's naval forces lay mines in the waterway to try to block it.
Two Singapore-registered container vessels were hit this week by "unknown projectiles,"
according to the Singaporean Maritime and Port Authority.
The ships were transiting the Strait of Hormuz.
One sank and the other reached safety.
Officials said no injuries were reported.
Hadil Al-Shelchi, NPR News, Istanbul.
Ukraine says it's going to start attacking Russian oil refineries again.
President Trump had told Ukraine not to do this.
Trump also claimed Russia had agreed to a cease-fire on striking energy targets, but
Russia never stopped.
President Trump got back to the White House only a couple of hours ago.
He's been on a Western campaign swing.
He attended a rally last night in Kalispell, Montana.
There he announced the U.S. will build a new military testing range that Montana Republican
lawmakers have requested.
Trump has been holding rallies in states that typically vote for Republicans.
NPR's Tamara Keith says that is different from trying to bolster Republicans in states
that typically back Democrats.
Most of these stops aren't just about feeling the warm embrace of an adoring rally crowd.
The map of competitive House and Senate races includes a lot of states and districts Trump
won by healthy margins just two years ago.
Republicans are playing defense in Alaska, Texas, Iowa, Ohio, and now even Kansas.
NPR's Tamara Keith reporting.
A group of swing voters in Georgia who supported President Trump in 2024 has largely changed
its view of him, and they say their frustration and disappointment is influencing who they
vote for during this year's midterm elections.
NPR's Ashley Lopez reports.
NPR observed focus groups with 12 voters in Georgia who voted for President Biden in 2020
and Trump in 2024.
11 now say they disapprove of the overall job Trump has been doing and 10 say they regret
voting for him.
Cynthia, an independent voter who participated under the condition her last name would not
be used, says this frustration is affecting how she's going to vote.
People that are aligned closely with him, I would not vote for because I haven't supported
what he's done so far, and it's like I said, it's been a very big disappointment.
So I would probably lean toward people that are not aligned with him to vote for.
Many said they hope a mix of power in Washington will create some stability.
Ashley Lopez, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Online streamer Netflix says it's going to lay off about 6% of its workforce.
That is about 1000 positions.
Other forecasters say the dangerous Santa Ana winds are returning to Northern California.
These winds can trigger wildfires, and in the past, some of the fires have been deadly
and very destructive.
The National Weather Service has posted red flag warnings for much of California today.
The Weather Service is cautioning high winds and very dry conditions can help spark new
fires.
The faculty senate at Cornell University met yesterday.
They've started a no-confidence process on university leadership.
NPR's Alyssa Nadworney reports it's over the handling of an allegation of campus sexual
assault two years ago.
University President Michael Kotlikoff joined the faculty meeting to take questions and
talk about what the school is doing to address safety on campus.
But faculty still went ahead on beginning a no-confidence vote, which is expected in
a few weeks.
It's an opportunity to voice their dissatisfaction with the administration, but ultimately, Kotlikoff's
job will be in the hands of the Board of Trustees, a group that includes donors and alumni.
They'll be meeting on campus starting Thursday.
Alyssa Nadworney, NPR News Ithaca, New York.
The Vatican says that Pope Leo has spent a good second night at a hospital in Rome.
Leo had surgery two days ago, doctors removed the lower part of his right lung to address
cancer.
The Vatican says Leo is eating, he's up and walking, and his condition is progressing
normally.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Iran attacks ships in the Strait of Hormuz, sinking one Singapore-registered vessel after a naval mine strike
Ukraine says it will resume attacks on Russian oil refineries despite Trump's warning
Trump holds rally in Kalispell, Montana, announces new military testing range requested by Montana Republicans
Republicans playing defense in Alaska, Texas, Iowa, Ohio, and Kansas House and Senate races
Georgia swing voters who backed Trump in 2024 say disappointment will shape their midterm votes
Netflix to lay off about 6% of its workforce, roughly 1,000 positions
Red flag warnings issued across much of California as Santa Ana winds return
Cornell University faculty senate begins no-confidence process against administration over handling of sexual assault allegation
Pope Leo recovering normally in Rome hospital after surgery to remove part of his right lung
